searchText: > Received goodbye request from 16Uiu2HAmAQE5mrh46ErJqEvW4MK6koKkWycV8oJBneC5pWbemgWC, reason=129 Whats reason 129? Not part of the spec, but I know teku uses it to state that they are 'full', and so are not accepting new peers ah, tnx Yes, can confirm that Teku uses the 129 reason for "too many peers". <@!573787335796326400> Seems like teku doesn't return status response when there is "129" situation Is that by design? I see in logs I've sent status request, and I get from that peer goodbye request with 129 and no response for status <@!545555441518772225> sorry, I need to defer to someone who actually understands the networking for the actual mechanics of that. Tagging <@!340345049063882753> for when the sun next rises in Australia... sure 🙂 <@!545555441518772225> I suspect we disconnect before we ever read the status request. We check if we've exceeded maximum peer count as soon as the libp2p handshake completes. It may be worth being more forgiving about this so we start showing up in node crawling stats which never seem to find us.
